evidence_packet.summary: Sharon Uche, 24, from Manchester says the Anthony Walker Bursary Scheme has given her confidence
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A woman who has been supported to train as a barrister by a bursary which honours a murdered teenager has said she wants to become a "hard-working" prosecutor who "treats witnesses with care" Sharon Uche, 24, from Manchester, said being chosen for the Anthony Walker Bursary Scheme, which supports aspiring lawyers from under-represented backgrounds, had given her the confidence to "reach my goals" and "opened doors" The bursary is a tribute to 18-year-old Anthony, who had ambitions to study law but was murdered in a racist attack on Merseyside in 2005 Uche said she had been inspired by his family's fight for justice and wanted to draw on Anthony's own values when building her career Anthony's mother, Dr Gee Walker, set up a foundation in her son's name to tackle racism, hate crime and discrimination In partnership with the CPS and the National Black Crown Prosecution Association, the foundation offers an Anthony Walker Bursary - as well as a mentor - to help aspiring lawyers from under-represented Black, Asian and minority ethnic backgrounds in the north-west of England

title: Couple share secret to keeping 70-year romance alive

evidence_packet.title: Couple share secret to keeping 70-year romance alive
evidence_packet.lead: Meet Colin and Carol Hill from Cleveleys who are still loved up after 70 years of wedded bliss
evidence_packet.summary: Meet Colin and Carol Hill from Cleveleys who are still loved up after 70 years of wedded bliss
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Colin and Carol Hill's love story began on the dance floor more than 70 years ago. Now in their nineties, they still play table tennis and attend keep-fit classes, and say staying active has helped keep their romance alive Colin, 91, and Carol, 90, from Cleveleys, married two years after meeting at the historic Hill Stores Ballroom in Oldham in 1954 Colin walked Carol home after their first dance and declared he was going to marry her. Her response was simple: "No way." However, Colin won her over and, more than seven decades later, the couple say they are as much in love now as they were as newlyweds Reflecting on their platinum anniversary, husband Colin said he felt "blessed" to have had Carol by his side He said the secret to their marriage was "respecting each other", and added that his wife still looked "a million dollars"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Over the course of four years, student Bilal Kazi manipulated and groomed at least 70 girls from across the UK - but police fear there could be more than 100 further victims yet to be identified Kazi, who was aged between 22 and 26 at the time, led his victims to believe they were in a relationship with a 14-year-old boy named Reece Kazi, 27, was sentenced to 30 years in prison last week after pleading guilty to 37 charges including making indecent images, blackmail and inciting a child to engage in sexual activity The lead detective in the case, Det Con Georgia Hughes, said his crimes came to light only after one of the victims was "brave enough to go and report what had happened" Kazi, who was a student from India studying at the University of Chester, would meet his victims online - most notably on Snapchat, Wink, and Roblox - always using the same method He provided a false photograph of a boy - who has not been identified - to aid his deception between August 2021 and August 2025

title: Scouts say they face £1m tourist tax cost for overnight trips

evidence_packet.title: Scouts say they face £1m tourist tax cost for overnight trips
evidence_packet.lead: The increased cost after the proposed Visitors Levy is imposed could price some young people out of joining Scout camps and other trips, the group said
evidence_packet.summary: The increased cost after the proposed Visitors Levy is imposed could price some young people out of joining Scout camps and other trips, the group said
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The overnight levy would allow councils and regional authorities to charge visitors an additional fee for their accommodation, including campsites, raising money to be spent on local services The increased cost from the Visitors Levy could price some young people out of joining Scout camps and other trips, the group said Dwayne Fields, the UK's Chief Scout, has called for youth groups to be exempted and said the charity - which sees more than 1.4m overnight stays a year - would be "firmly opposed to any proposal that would see local mayors tax Scouts and other voluntary youth organisations" The Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government told the BBC that local leaders who introduce the levy "will have the option to exempt certain types of accommodation in their areas, including accommodation which is often used for trips by youth groups like Scouts and Girl They added money raised from the levy will "stay local and be invested in the visitor experience and local growth including in high streets, parks and events" Labour mayors have indicated they would cap the levy at 5% but the legislation contains no maximum limit

title: 'I didn't want to move from Seven Sisters flats - but now I'm delighted'

evidence_packet.title: 'I didn't want to move from Seven Sisters flats - but now I'm delighted'
evidence_packet.lead: Andrew Kowalczyk had lived in a tower block in Rochdale for 27 years and now calls a bungalow home
evidence_packet.summary: Andrew Kowalczyk had lived in a tower block in Rochdale for 27 years and now calls a bungalow home
evidence_packet.evidence_text: 'I didn't want to move from Seven Sisters flats - but now I'm delighted' - BBC News Image caption, Andrew Kowalczyk lived on the College Bank estate for 27 years but says he is now happy in his new home By Richard Stead North West Published 21 November 2026 After 27 years living in the Seven Sisters tower blocks in Rochdale, Andrew Kowalczyk did not want to leave. But he said he felt the demolition of the flats, which have dominated the town's skyline since the 1960s, was "inevitable" and he was now relieved to have been rehoused. Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) announced last week that the blocks would be bulldozed and replaced with a new College Bank estate of about 600 homes. It comes after a 10-year campaign by residents who wanted the flats to be refurbished and not knocked down but RBH said the demolition was the only "realistic" option. Kowalczyk, 61, who lived in the Mardyke block, said he was reluctant to move out of his "secure" home and the "great views" but he has since been rehomed in a bungalow in Lower Falinge and was now "delighted with it". Residents started to move out of the flats in October last year after long-term safety concerns were raised in October last year. The blocks are almost all empty, with 78 homes out of 766 currently occupied. Some of the remaining tenants have vowed to challenge the demolition decision. But Kowalczyk said: "I didn't want to move from College Bank because you had great views and your home was secure but I knew that - no matter how much we resisted - demolition is bound to happen. "When I looked at my new bungalow in Lower Falinge, it was really clean, there were new tiles, it also had new cupboards, so I made my mind up about moving in really quickly and now I'm delighted with it." Image source, Rochdale Boroughwide

title: Hulme Hippodrome campaigners want to buy theatre after no sale at auction

evidence_packet.title: Hulme Hippodrome campaigners want to buy theatre after no sale at auction
evidence_packet.lead: Hulme Hippodrome was listed at auction on Thursday but failed to sell
evidence_packet.summary: Hulme Hippodrome was listed at auction on Thursday but failed to sell
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Locals who have campaigned to try to save a historical theatre from demolition say they want to buy it after it failed to sell at auction Hulme Hippodrome in Manchester was listed for a reserve price of £895,000, but on Thursday bidding failed to reach that mark The Grade II-listed building was last used for theatre in the 1960s, and has since hosted live recordings of BBC shows, bingo events, and a church congregation. It has been left empty since 2017 Paul Baker, from the Save Hulme Hippodrome campaign group, said they had been "chasing this building for five years" because it represents "working-class culture in this city" so he was "really pleased" it was still available "We thought the price was too high, and so didn't think it was going to get sold," he told BBC Radio Manchester Baker said the group had since decided to investigate whether its members could raise the money needed to bring the theatre into community ownership

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Over the course of four years, student Bilal Kazi manipulated and groomed at least 70 girls from across the UK - but police fear there could be more than 100 further victims yet to be identified Kazi, who was aged between 22 and 26 at the time, led his victims to believe they were in a relationship with a 14-year-old boy named Reece Kazi, 27, was sentenced to 30 years in prison last week after pleading guilty to 37 charges including making indecent images, blackmail and inciting a child to engage in sexual activity The lead detective in the case, Det Con Georgia Hughes, said his crimes came to light only after one of the victims was "brave enough to go and report what had happened" Kazi, who was a student from India studying at the University of Chester, would meet his victims online - most notably on Snapchat, Wink, and Roblox - always using the same method He provided a false photograph of a boy - who has not been identified - to aid his deception between August 2021 and August 2025

She was 84 Born in Oldham, Greater Manchester, she had lived in Wickham Skeith, in Suffolk, with her late husband Peter Handford From 2004 until 2019, she was also an ambassador for East Anglia's Children's Hospices (EACH). The charity said it was "deeply saddened" by her death and would "remember her with enormous fondness and gratitude" "Helen was very special to us and a wonderful ambassador, supporter and friend who worked tirelessly to champion our cause," a spokesperson said "Whether fundraising, attending events, opening our shops or rallying our volunteers, Helen brought incredible warmth, empathy and joy

title: Scouts say they face £1m tourist tax cost for overnight trips

evidence_packet.title: Scouts say they face £1m tourist tax cost for overnight trips
evidence_packet.lead: The overnight levy would allow councils and regional authorities to charge visitors an additional fee for their accommodation, including campsites, raising money to be spent on local services The increased cost from the Visitors Levy could price some young people out of joining S
evidence_packet.summary: The overnight levy would allow councils and regional authorities to charge visitors an additional fee for their accommodation, including campsites, raising money to be spent on local services The increased cost from the Visitors Levy could price some young people out of joining S
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The overnight levy would allow councils and regional authorities to charge visitors an additional fee for their accommodation, including campsites, raising money to be spent on local services The increased cost from the Visitors Levy could price some young people out of joining Scout camps and other trips, the group said Dwayne Fields, the UK's Chief Scout, has called for youth groups to be exempted and said the charity - which sees more than 1.4m overnight stays a year - would be "firmly opposed to any proposal that would see local mayors tax Scouts and other voluntary youth organisations" The Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government told the BBC that local leaders who introduce the levy "will have the option to exempt certain types of accommodation in their areas, including accommodation which is often used for trips by youth groups like Scouts and Girl They added money raised from the levy will "stay local and be invested in the visitor experience and local growth including in high streets, parks and events" Labour mayors have indicated they would cap the levy at 5% but the legislation contains no maximum limit

evidence_packet.evidence_text: After 27 years living in the Seven Sisters tower blocks in Rochdale, Andrew Kowalczyk did not want to leave But he said he felt the demolition of the flats, which have dominated the town's skyline since the 1960s, was "inevitable" and he was now relieved to have been rehoused Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) announced last week that the blocks would be bulldozed and replaced with a new College Bank estate of about 600 homes It comes after a 10-year campaign by residents who wanted the flats to be refurbished and not knocked down but RBH said the demolition was the only "realistic" option Kowalczyk, 61, who lived in the Mardyke block, said he was reluctant to move out of his "secure" home and the "great views" but he has since been rehomed in a bungalow in Lower Falinge and was now "delighted with it" Residents started to move out of the flats in October last year after long-term safety concerns were raised in October last year

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Locals who have campaigned to try to save a historical theatre from demolition say they want to buy it after it failed to sell at auction Hulme Hippodrome in Manchester was listed for a reserve price of £895,000, but on Thursday bidding failed to reach that mark The Grade II-listed building was last used for theatre in the 1960s, and has since hosted live recordings of BBC shows, bingo events, and a church congregation. It has been left empty since 2017 Paul Baker, from the Save Hulme Hippodrome campaign group, said they had been "chasing this building for five years" because it represents "working-class culture in this city" so he was "really pleased" it was still available "We thought the price was too high, and so didn't think it was going to get sold," he told BBC Radio Manchester Baker said the group had since decided to investigate whether its members could raise the money needed to bring the theatre into community ownership

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Police say they are determined to get justice for a baby whose remains were found two years ago The infant, named Ava by Greater Manchester Police, was discovered by a dog walker near Ashtons Field, in Little Hulton, Salford, on 20 November 2024 Despite a long-running investigation and a £50,000 reward put up by the Greater Manchester combined authority, detectives have still not been able to identify the child's mother Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said its determination to find the answers "has never wavered", and that it wanted to "secure the justice that Ava deserves" Det Insp Louise Kelly said: "We know 20 November will be particularly significant for Ava's parents, family members, and anyone who may have known her." The organisation warned they could face a £1 million annual bill as a result of the levy, which one Manchester troupe leader dubbed the 'tent tax' Ministers have said local areas will be able to decide on exemptions but the Scout Association has called for an explicit England-wide commitment to spare youth groups from the charge. The Visitor Levy Bill will give mayors and local leaders the ability to introduce a fee on over Labour regional mayors have indicated they will cap the levy at 5% but there is no maximum limit in the legislation. The Scout Association warned the tax they would face could cost the charity £1 million across the country, based on a 5% charge on the 1,423,344 annual overnight s Chief Scout Dwayne Fields said: "We strongly support investment being made available to strengthen local communities. Well-crafted legislation can unlock that opportunity "But we are firmly opposed to any proposal that would see local mayors tax Scouts and other voluntary youth organisations for camping trips that equip young people with skills for life, while burdening volunteers with the role of unpaid government tax collectors."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Greater Manchester council 'embarrassingly' forgot to show what £1m of taxpayer cash was spent on An investigation by the Manchester Evening News has revealed that the council failed to publish mandatory transparency records for staff procureme Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 06:33, 22 Nov 2026 An investigation has revealed a Greater Manchester council 'embarrassingly' forgot to show what £1m of taxpayer cash was spent on by council staff Some councils across the country use government procurement cards , sometimes referred to as p-cards, for low-value and ad-hoc purchases. They have been described as 'essentially a company credit card' used by eligible council staff They can be used to make emergency payments, reduce paperwork, and speed up purchases from suppliers. However under local government transparency rules introduced in 2015, councils across the country who use them are required to publish what payments have been made to reassure pe Oldham council have now admitted they have not been revealing how these cards were being used and what taxpayer money has been spent on for eleven years. This is after no public records for payments were found by the Manchester Evening News The council is now working on publishing seven years' worth of payment records, which is understood to be the length of time this data is required to be kept. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Scouts fear Andy Burnham's tourist tax could price kids out of camping trips A Manchester Scout leader dubbed the levy the 'tent tax' Add to preferred sources Comments News Damon Wilkinson Reporter and David Hughes Press Association Polit Scout groups fear Andy Burnham's tourist tax could price some kids out of camping trips. The organisation warned they could face a £1 million annual bill as a result of the levy, which one Manchester troupe leader dubbed the 'tent tax' Ministers have said local areas will be able to decide on exemptions but the Scout Association has called for an explicit England-wide commitment to spare youth groups from the charge. The Visitor Levy Bill will give mayors and local leaders the ability to introduce a fee on over Labour regional mayors have indicated they will cap the levy at 5% but there is no maximum limit in the legislation. The Scout Association warned the tax they would face could cost the charity £1 million across the country, based on a 5% charge on the 1,423,344 annual overnight s Chief Scout Dwayne Fields said: "We strongly support investment being made available to strengthen local communities. Well-crafted legislation can unlock that opportunity "But we are firmly opposed to any proposal that would see local mayors tax Scouts and other voluntary youth organisations for camping trips that equip young people with skills for life, while burdening volunteers with the role of unpaid government tax collectors."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Greater Manchester council 'embarrassingly' forgot to show what £1m of taxpayer cash was spent on An investigation by the Manchester Evening News has revealed that the council failed to publish mandatory transparency records for staff procureme Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 06:33, 22 Nov 2026 An investigation has revealed a Greater Manchester council 'embarrassingly' forgot to show what £1m of taxpayer cash was spent on by council staff Some councils across the country use government procurement cards , sometimes referred to as p-cards, for low-value and ad-hoc purchases. They have been described as 'essentially a company credit card' used by eligible council staff They can be used to make emergency payments, reduce paperwork, and speed up purchases from suppliers. However under local government transparency rules introduced in 2015, councils across the country who use them are required to publish what payments have been made to reassure pe Oldham council have now admitted they have not been revealing how these cards were being used and what taxpayer money has been spent on for eleven years. This is after no public records for payments were found by the Manchester Evening News The council is now working on publishing seven years' worth of payment records, which is understood to be the length of time this data is required to be kept. Over this period, over £1m was spent by council and school staff

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Scouts fear Andy Burnham's tourist tax could price kids out of camping trips A Manchester Scout leader dubbed the levy the 'tent tax' Add to preferred sources Comments News Damon Wilkinson Reporter and David Hughes Press Association Polit Scout groups fear Andy Burnham's tourist tax could price some kids out of camping trips. The organisation warned they could face a £1 million annual bill as a result of the levy, which one Manchester troupe leader dubbed the 'tent tax' Ministers have said local areas will be able to decide on exemptions but the Scout Association has called for an explicit England-wide commitment to spare youth groups from the charge. The Visitor Levy Bill will give mayors and local leaders the ability to introduce a fee on over Labour regional mayors have indicated they will cap the levy at 5% but there is no maximum limit in the legislation. The Scout Association warned the tax they would face could cost the charity £1 million across the country, based on a 5% charge on the 1,423,344 annual overnight s Chief Scout Dwayne Fields said: "We strongly support investment being made available to strengthen local communities. Well-crafted legislation can unlock that opportunity "But we are firmly opposed to any proposal that would see local mayors tax Scouts and other voluntary youth organisations for camping trips that equip young people with skills for life, while burdening volunteers with the role of unpaid government tax collectors."

It is being called a 'loophole' Ahmed has been stripped of his British citizenship, leaving him solely as a Pakistani national Following his release, Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said her intention was to change the legal loophole to make it possible to deport those convicted of serious crimes , including terrorism and child sexual exploitation. His health had significantly deteriorated in the years prior to his death. He had become immobile and bed bound prior to his death due to his profound neurological disability Examination of his brain following his death confirmed an in life diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease In addition, he was found to have high stage chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), stage 3 Limbic-predominant age related TPD-43 encephalopathy (LATE) and small vessel cerebrovascular disease. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport’s annual Autumn Leaves lunches were held on Wednesday and Thursday this week, with more than 150 over-65s from the Wythenshawe and Woodhouse Park areas enjoying a free hot meal, entertainment and the chance to socialise The annual event, which is open to over-65s from Woodhouse Park and other wards neighbouring the airport, is staffed by volunteers from Manchester Airport – who waited tables, served at the bar and dished up a slap-up three course meal, accompanied by a live performance from The The staff who arranged the lunches were taking part in a scheme the airport operates allowing colleagues to claim up to two working days per year, on full pay, to support good causes that matter to them in areas neighbouring the airport Since it started in 2011, the event – which is hosted at the Woodhouse Park Lifestyle Centre – has served more than 3,000 over-65s, and helped to forge countless friendships and social connections among a demographic that is statistically at the highest risk for loneliness and so Cllr Rob Nunney, who represents the Woodhouse Park ward on Manchester City Council, was present at the event and said: “I want to thank Manchester Airport for putting this event on. It’s a fantastic way of giving back to the community and it’s so great to see so many people havin Attendee Elizabeth Bracken said: “I loved it. The afternoon was wonderful – the food, the service, the ambiance, I absolutely could not fault it at all and am already looking forward to next year.”

evidence_packet.title: Suffolk's Bad Girls legend Helen Fraser has died at aged 84

evidence_packet.summary: The actress, who also appeared in episodes of Coronation Street and The Royle Family, reportedly died on 10 November at Yaxley House Care Home, in Eye, Suffolk. She was 84 Born in Oldham, Greater Manchester, she had lived in Wickham Skeith, in Suffolk, with her late husband Peter
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The actress, who also appeared in episodes of Coronation Street and The Royle Family, reportedly died on 10 November at Yaxley House Care Home, in Eye, Suffolk. She was 84 Born in Oldham, Greater Manchester, she had lived in Wickham Skeith, in Suffolk, with her late husband Peter Handford From 2004 until 2019, she was also an ambassador for East Anglia's Children's Hospices (EACH). The charity said it was "deeply saddened" by her death and would "remember her with enormous fondness and gratitude" "Helen was very special to us and a wonderful ambassador, supporter and friend who worked tirelessly to champion our cause," a spokesperson said "Whether fundraising, attending events, opening our shops or rallying our volunteers, Helen brought incredible warmth, empathy and joy "She had a wonderful way with people and made a lasting impression on all those fortunate enough to spend time in her company."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The infant, named Ava by Greater Manchester Police, was discovered by a dog walker near Ashtons Field, in Little Hulton, Salford, on 20 November 2024 Despite a long-running investigation and a £50,000 reward put up by the Greater Manchester combined authority, detectives have still not been able to identify the child's mother Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said its determination to find the answers "has never wavered", and that it wanted to "secure the justice that Ava deserves" Det Insp Louise Kelly said: "We know 20 November will be particularly significant for Ava's parents, family members, and anyone who may have known her." She added: "Behind every line of enquiry, every review of evidence, and every piece of information we assess is a baby girl who will never be forgotten." Kelly said the force was currently trying to organise a funeral for Ava

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The seafood and cocktail bar and Champagne-led tasting menu restaurant have both caught the attention of Michelin’s inspectors… Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Two more Manchester restaurants have been added to the Michelin Guide, with Bar Shrimp and Portfolio both making the cut in its November update The two city centre spots are markedly different propositions, but both are the work of teams already well acquainted with the Michelin Guide Part seafood restaurant, part cocktail bar and part late-night music spot, Bar Shrimp brings together the team’s collective obsessions with sustainably sourced seafood, great drinks and records With its David Lynch-inspired red velvet interiors and Mastersounds sound system, the bar serves everything from oysters and caviar to smoked fish croquettes, alongside an inventive cocktail list Its next-door sister restaurant, Higher Ground, was added to the Michelin Guide in September 2023, just seven months after opening, going on to secure a Bib Gourmand in January 2024

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Counter Manchester , the much-anticipated new restaurant from Open Restaurant Group , opens its doors today at 12pm. It is the group’s first opening in Manchester city centre and brings a theatrical approach to dining to the heart of the city Led by acclaimed chef Andrew Sheridan, Counter is located in Manchester’s Island Building on John Dalton Street and has 60 covers. It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. evidence_packet.lead: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities.
evidence_packet.summary: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

After one win in 10 Premier League games, the manager was sacked, and new head coach Pochettino was poached from the USMNT It has been a hectic few days for the former Spurs and Chelsea boss. He was flown in via private jet in the early hours of Wednesday after overseeing one last game for the US against Haiti on Tuesday. He then took training on Thursday, which was subject to controversy after part That session will be one of only three Pochettino can oversee with his new players before he heads to Anfield on Sunday. Ex-Everton man Ferguson thinks that this prep is far from ideal when facing a bitter rival in a huge televised clash Get the best United news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the Manchester Evening News!

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Serious concerns raised following death of Manchester United great Nobby Stiles 'In my opinion there is a risk that future deaths could occur unless action is taken' Add to preferred sources Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 10:03, 21 Nov 2 A coroner has written to the Football Association and the government warning of the dangers of heading balls following the death of Manchester United and England great Nobby Stiles. The Collyhurst-born 1966 World Cup winner died in 2020 aged 78 The report references 'amateur or professional adults and children' and a 'risk' of them developing a brain disease 'in the future' An inquest into Stiles' death heard an examination of his brain revealed that along with Alzheimer's Disease, he had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) - a progressive brain disease linked to repeated head injuries or blows to the head Senior coroner Alison Mutch, sitting at Stockport Coroners' Court, ruled the CTE had 'significantly contributed' to his death and that she was 'entirely satisfied' the reason he developed the condition was due to 'repeated heading of the ball' Now Ms Mutch has officially raised a series of concerns to prevent future deaths.
